# Review — iliad-045 (7.379–482)

## Pass 1 (units)

Checked in order: every grammatical label and every claim about where a word stands, against the line; every cross-reference against the published parts in the repository root (iliad-001–044, odyssey-001–120) and the two house tables; Greek → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; remembered English in `i`; quotation marks and `mark`; the packet's flagged lines (none); mechanics (`t` joined reproduces the packet's 104 lines; one `\n` in `l` per `\n` in `t`; no `\n` in `i`; no backticks or ASCII apostrophes anywhere; notes under ~110 words; `p` on all nine ¶ units: 379, 398, 403, 412, 421, 433, 442, 454, 464). Speech framing: the previous part (iliad-044) closes Priam's speech with ” at 378, so 379 rightly opens without a mark; the five speeches here (Idaeus 385–397, Diomedes 400–402, Agamemnon 406–411, Poseidon 446–453, Zeus 455–463) each carry “ on the first unit, ” on the last, and a `mark` on the first. No speech runs into the next part (482 is the end of Book 7). `t` was not touched. All edits made by script.

### Findings considered and refused

- 448 n, "κλειτός is κλυτός ‘famous’": an etymological shortcut, but the Iliad table's own row (3.451) states "κλειτός = κλυτός", so the note follows the house. Left.
- 394, αἴ κ’ ἐθέλητε as "whether you are willing" where 376 had "if they are willing": after ἠνώγεον εἰπεῖν the clause is the content of the word to be spoken and reads as an indirect question; the drafter's new-renderings row gives the reason. Defensible; left.
- 433 and 459, cut at a comma: each period would otherwise run 433–437 and 459–463, five lines; the rule allows the cut. Left.
- 443 `l` "beside Zeus the lightning-flasher seated" against 4.1's "seated beside Zeus": only a half-line is shared and ἀστεροπητῇ falls between the words; `i` keeps "seated beside Zeus". Left.
- 409 `l` "of the dead, of those who have died, once they have died": the doubling is Homer's (κατατεθνηώτων … ἐπεί κε θάνωσι) and the first phrase is the Odyssey's fixed English. Left.
- 417 `l` "for both tasks": "tasks" is supplied for the adverbial ἀμφότερον, and the note says the Greek has no noun. Left.
- 479 `l`/`i` close with ";" where odyssey-059 has "." (the Greek has an ano teleia here, a full stop there): the validator will warn, as the drafter predicted; the stop follows the edition. Left.
- 386 ἠνώγει singular with Πρίαμός τε καὶ ἄλλοι Τρῶες: the note's "agreeing with the nearer subject" is the standard account. Left.
- 7.401 γνωτόν as the neuter adjective, not "kinsman": correct; the homograph is named. Left.
- 7.449 `l` "a wall have built as a wall above the ships": awkward but deliberate (both noun and verb kept visible, the sense given in `i` and the note). Left.
- 7.446 `i` "now … still" for one ἔτι: a light doubling that reads naturally. Left.

Scansion flags: none in the packet; nothing to scan by hand.

### Findings considered and refused

- Broadened entries over 230 characters (πάρα 477, ἐπ 650, τοῦ 374, ποτὶ 247, αὐτὴν 238, ἔλθοι 232): the published entry must be kept whole and several were already past the limit before this part; the limit is applied to new entries, and each addition was kept to one clause. Left.
- κέλονται "(Attic κελεύουσι)": κέλομαι is a distinct poetic verb, but the parenthesis gives the Attic equivalent in sense, which is what the format asks for. Left.
- θηεῦντο lemmatised θεάομαι with "Ionic θηεῦντο": LSJ heads the verb θεάομαι and gives θηέομαι as the epic form; the unit's note names θηέομαι and the Attic form, so the two agree. Left.
- μέθυ "object of ἀγέμεν", ἰδαῖον "object of προσέφη", and the "agreeing with X" tags: these name the construction rather than a line and match the published glossary's practice (e.g. the shipped αἴθωνι, χεῖράς). Left.
- ὤφελλ lemma "ὀφέλλω (ὀφείλω)": LSJ gives ὀφέλλω as the epic form of ὀφείλω; consistent with the unit's note. Left.
- ἀκούεις listed as novel though common: the form is new to the Iliad glossary; correct as novel. Left.
- Known forms checked and found covered without broadening: τὸ (relative), ὃς (relative at 401, 457), ἀγέμεν, πρίν, ἔγρετο, ἄκριτον (agreeing with τύμβον), ἐφῆπται, πείρατ’, ἀμφότερον, ἔνθεν, ἄγρει, ὕπερ (anastrophe), ἀγασσάμενοι (’wonder at’ present), ἀγγελίην, κήομεν, νέον, λαός, τοι, σφιν, ὕλην, ἅλα, τάφρον, ἔτλη, πιέειν, ἐπεί κε, ὅτι, ὥς κε, ὡς (’that’; wish with ὤφελλ’), ἦ (interrogative), ἤτοι, εἰν, ὄρωρε, ἄμμε, ἀκήν, ὅρκια, εἶλαρ, πονέοντο, πάρ, μύθων ἦρχε, ὅσον, ἐπικίδναται, πολλόν, μένος, αὖτις, κλισίας, τάς, βοήν, νεκύων, ἱρήν, ἔβαν, ἦμος, πω, θ’, ἀραρυίας, εἴη, δόσαν, ὀχθήσας, οἷον, σέο, ὅτ’ ἂν, ὑπ’ + dat. of the father, ᾕρει, μεγαίρω, σιωπῇ.
